assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario reading

2.17 is the trailing-`?` TEXT path, not a structured ask-user tool. Its own
description is explicit: "Agent's reply ends in a question mark, signalling
it's waiting for user input. Validates the trailing-? path through the state
classifier (session.IsWaitingForUserInput -> state_classifier.go decision 2a).
The recipe deliberately stops at the waiting episode and does not answer the
question." The user-observable arc this cell asserts is therefore
`ready -> working -> waiting`, with the waiting episode visible and no
skip-over back to ready. That is the same reading claudecode, codex, kiro-cli,
mistral-vibe and pi are assessed under.

## agent - yes

Hermes has NO AskUserQuestion-style structured blocking-question primitive:
`git grep -n "ask_user|AskUser|elicit"` over the installed source
(`/Users/ingo/hermes-local/.hermes/hermes-agent`, v0.19.0) returns only
`agent/codex_responses_adapter.py` (re-elicit a proper *tool call*, unrelated)
and `agent/transports/codex_app_server_session.py:1028`
(`mcpServer/elicitation/request`, the ACP/app-server transport, not the CLI
turn loop). Under the structured-tool reading this cell would be `no` - that is
what opencode's sibling cell froze on.

Under THIS scenario's reading the verdict is `yes`, and it is not a
plausibility argument: the live store already contains the exact shape. Two
`role='assistant' active=1 finish_reason='stop'` rows hold content that is a
literal question - `20260726_185601_4811e3` "Hello! How can I help you today?"
and `20260726_190232_65c19a` "Hi! How can I help?". Both are ordinary
end-of-turn rows, so Hermes ends a turn on a question mark exactly the way the
scenario asks, and `content` is plain text (not a structured block list), which
is what `Parser.ParseLine` reads.

Passing these through the shipped detector: `splitSentences` yields "Hello!" +
"How can I help you today?"; the trailing sentence ends in `?`, is not
rhetorical (`isRhetorical` needs a following because/since sentence), so
`ExtractQuestionSnippet` returns non-empty and `ProseIndicatesWaiting` is true.

## daemon - full

The chain from a Hermes store row to a user-visible `waiting` is complete in
today's code, with no missing seam:

1. `Parser.ParseLine` (parser.go:81-95) on `role='assistant'` sets
   `ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text))`
   BEFORE truncation - the cue is computed on a 400-rune window
   (`MaxWaitingScanRunes = 2 * MaxAssistantTextRunes`), not on the 200-rune
   display tail, so a question sitting before the display cut is still seen
   (#1150). With `finish_reason='stop'` the same event's type becomes
   `turn_done`.
2. `foldMessages`/`messageFold.apply` (metrics.go:189-249) carries
   `pendingWaitingCue` alongside `lastAssistantText`, and resets it on the next
   `user_message` - the ProcessOwnedStore path bypasses the tailer, so that
   reset is re-implemented here on purpose. `querySessionMetrics` publishes it
   as `metrics.PendingWaitingCue` (metrics.go:137) and `LastEventType`
   (metrics.go:135).
3. `SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone()` (domain/session/metrics.go:532) is true on
   `LastEventType == "turn_done"` with no open tool call, so the classifier's
   `agent_done` rung fires.
4. `classifyAgentDone` (state_classifier.go:270-278) asks
   `IsWaitingForUserInput()` FIRST; that returns true on
   `m.PendingWaitingCue` (waiting_cue.go:81-83) and routes
   `-> waiting` ("turn ended with question or cue -> waiting") instead of
   `-> ready`. No hook, no tool, no idle heuristic is involved - which matters,
   because Hermes has no hook surface at all.

The `working` leg of the arc survives even the worst timing case. The watcher
polls every 2s (`defaultPollInterval`), so a fast turn can land the `user` row
AND the `assistant/stop` row between two scans - one activity event carrying
`LastEventType=turn_done` straight onto a `ready` session, which
`classifyAgentDone` would take directly `ready -> waiting`, skipping `working`.
`forceReadyToWorkingIfActive` (session_detector_activity.go:864-886) prevents
that: it runs after `RefreshOnActivity` and before `classifyAndTransition`, and
records a real `ready -> working` state_transition first. Its guard is
`transcriptGrew`, and for Hermes that is structurally true -
`observeTranscriptGrowth` (session_detector_activity.go:726-737) `os.Stat`s
`ev.TranscriptPath`, which for this adapter is the synthetic
`"<store>?session=<id>"`; the stat errors, and the function fails OPEN
(`transcriptGrew` stays true). So the working blip is emitted in both the
split-pass and the collapsed-pass regime.

Nothing downstream un-does the waiting. `agent.Event.Terminal` (set from
`turnIsDone`) only short-circuits the activity debounce
(session_detector_activity.go:467-475); it is not a state input. Driver
teardown does not manufacture a `ready` either: a dead PID goes through
`HandleProcessExit`, which DELETES the session (pid_manager.go:326-344) rather
than transitioning it - so the "no state_transition to ready" invariant on the
final phase is safe against the recipe's own exit.

## driver - ready

`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh:113` declares
`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`; this recipe needs `send`,
`wait_turn`, `sleep` only. Its `wait_turn` (driver:258) polls
`COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=... AND role='assistant' AND
finish_reason='stop'` and returns on an increase - a turn that ends on a
QUESTION is still a `finish_reason='stop'` row (both live question rows above
carry it), so the poll fires exactly once at the waiting boundary and does not
hang. `resolve_session_id` binds only to a session with
`started_at > <slot launch ts>`, so a stale row in the shared store cannot
satisfy the wait. Interactive is the right path: the REPL outlives the turn, so
the waiting classification lands inside the observation window instead of
racing process exit.

## What is NOT proven yet

The daemon verdict is code + live-store evidence, not a recording. Emission is
unusually well covered here for a doc-based assessment (the two question rows
above are real, stored, `finish_reason='stop'` rows), but the arc reaching the
websocket in this order and timing is what `record` settles.
caveats: PROVISIONAL daemon verdict: derived from adapter source + live SQLite store facts, not from a recording. No hermes events.jsonl exists yet; record promotes it from provisional to settled.

Scenario-reading divergence, called out so it is not re-litigated: hermes has NO structured AskUserQuestion-equivalent (verified by grep over the installed source - only an ACP/app-server 'mcpServer/elicitation/request' on a transport the CLI turn loop does not use). This cell is assessed under scenario 2.17's OWN description (the trailing-? TEXT path through session.IsWaitingForUserInput), which is also how claudecode/codex/kiro-cli/mistral-vibe/pi are assessed. opencode's sibling cell froze at agent_supports:no under the stricter structured-tool reading; if the dispatcher re-freezes 2.17 on that reading, hermes would become no/n-a/n-a too.

The waiting verdict rests on a prose HEURISTIC, not an explicit marker: ProseIndicatesWaiting over the trailing 400 runes. The recipe therefore pins the reply shape hard (exactly one short question, ending in '?', no other text, no tool call). If the model instead answers declaratively or wraps the question mid-paragraph beyond the scan window, the turn classifies ready and the turn_end_waiting phase fails - that is a recipe/prompt-compliance failure, not a daemon bug.

Tool-call risk: hermes ships a terminal tool and a tool-calling turn ends with finish_reason='tool_calls', which keeps the session working and blocks the driver's wait_turn until a later stop row. The prompt says 'do not call any tool' for that reason; a model that ignores it makes the run time out rather than mis-assert.

Late birth (inherited from the column, adapter.go:16-19 / basic-turn cell): the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after launch), so there is no store-derived ready birth at launch. The recording's ready birth comes from the processlifecycle scanner's transient proc-<PID> pre-session, so session_birth is anchored to start and left UNPINNED, and every later phase chains via same_session_as off turn_start rather than off the birth.

cwd fragility (inherited): `hermes chat` writes source='cli' rows, which carry no cwd (live store: 21/22 cli rows empty). Project binding and DiscoverPID both fall back to defaultLiveCWD, which requires EXACTLY ONE live non-service hermes process; a second interactive hermes session makes it ambiguous and the pid_bind phase plus the project link go missing.

model/cost deliberately unpinned: the recorded model depends on the config.yaml in whatever HERMES_HOME the run exports (the maintainer's home defaults to gpt-5.6-luna, which irrlicht's capacity table does price). Only tokens_nonzero is asserted; record should fill observations.model from the recording and may add cost_nonzero once the recorded model is known to be priced.

The onboarding rig still has no hermes-specific env wiring (no HERMES_HOME reference under tools/onboarding-factory/scripts), so the driver and the recording daemon must be given a matching HERMES_HOME out of band.

sources.note: Scenario description: 'Agent's reply ends in a question mark ... Validates the trailing-? path through the state classifier (session.IsWaitingForUserInput -> state_classifier.go decision 2a). The recipe deliberately stops at the waiting episode and does not answer the question.' Acceptance: ready -> working -> waiting; waiting episode user-visible; final state waiting.

role='assistant': ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text)) computed on the FULL text before TruncateAssistantText; finish_reason='stop' rewrites EventType to turn_done. This is the waiting-state path for this cell.

foldMessages replays rows through Parser; messageFold.apply carries pendingWaitingCue with lastAssistantText and clears it on the next user_message (the ProcessOwnedStore path bypasses the tailer, where that reset normally lives). querySessionMetrics publishes PendingWaitingCue + LastEventType onto SessionMetrics.

ProseIndicatesWaiting = ExtractQuestionSnippet OR ExtractWaitingCue; IsWaitingForUserInput returns true on m.PendingWaitingCue before falling back to the truncated LastAssistantText. WaitingScanWindow bounds the scan at 2x the display cap (tailer/parser.go:816).

agent_done rung fires on IsAgentDone(); classifyAgentDone checks IsWaitingForUserInput FIRST and routes to waiting ('turn ended with question or cue -> waiting') instead of ready. Rungs above it (permission prompt, user-blocking tool, open_tool_stalled, idle_prompt) are all inert for hermes - no hooks, no open tool on this turn.

IsAgentDone(): true on LastEventType == 'turn_done' with no open tool call - the explicit finish_reason='stop' boundary hermes provides, so no idle-flush seam sits between the turn end and the classification.

Terminal only short-circuits the activity debounce (not a state input). forceReadyToWorkingIfActive records a real ready->working BEFORE classifyAndTransition, guarded on transcriptGrew; observeTranscriptGrowth os.Stats ev.TranscriptPath, which for hermes is the synthetic '<store>?session=<id>' - the stat errors and it fails OPEN, so the working leg is emitted even when one 2s scan collapses the user row and the assistant stop row into a single pass.

A dead PID reaps via HandleProcessExit, which DELETES the session rather than transitioning it - so the recipe's own tmux teardown cannot produce the ready transition the final phase's invariant forbids.

Live store, read-only (sqlite3 'file:...?mode=ro'). 29 assistant rows with active=1 AND finish_reason='stop'; 2 of them end in '?' - 20260726_185601_4811e3 'Hello! How can I help you today?' and 20260726_190232_65c19a 'Hi! How can I help?'. Direct emission evidence: hermes stores a question-ending turn as an ordinary stop row with plain-text content. Recent cli sessions run model gpt-5.6-luna with an empty cwd.

git grep -n 'ask_user|AskUser|elicit' over agent/*.py + cli.py returns only codex_responses_adapter.py (re-elicit a tool call) and transports/codex_app_server_session.py:1028 (mcpServer/elicitation/request on the ACP app-server transport). No structured ask-user tool in the CLI turn loop - which is why this cell rests on the trailing-? prose path.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn" covers every step this recipe needs. wait_turn polls COUNT(*) of assistant rows with finish_reason='stop' for the bound session - a question-ending turn carries that same finish_reason, so the poll fires at the waiting boundary instead of hanging.
Sibling cell in the same column; its late-birth / unpinned-session_birth anchoring and its cwd + HERMES_HOME preconditions are reused here for the same reasons.
Reference spec for this scenario: ready birth -> working -> waiting, stopping at the waiting episode without a follow-up reply.

preconditions: hermes v0.19.0+ on PATH with a provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml plus credentials, so a single prompt completes without an auth prompt
HERMES_HOME exported to the SAME recording home for both the driver and the recording daemon (the rig has no hermes env wiring today), so the daemon polls the store the run actually writes
sqlite3 on PATH - hermes writes no transcript, so the driver's session resolution and wait_turn read state.db directly

no OTHER interactive hermes session live during the run: source='cli' rows carry no cwd, so the adapter's live-process CWD fallback needs exactly one non-service hermes process to bind the project and discover the PID
irrlichd recording with the hermes store watcher enabled and the 'store' permission granted (IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all on a fresh home)
setup: The interactive driver launches `hermes chat` under tmux in a fresh per-run cwd and polls the pane for 'Type your message or /help' before typing - the TUI swallows keystrokes sent during its boot
The slot's transcript path is '<store>?session=<id>' (no transcript file exists); the session id is resolved from the sessions table after the first send, because the row does not exist at launch

The prompt pins the reply to exactly one short question ending in '?', with no other text and no tool call: the waiting verdict comes from the prose heuristic over the trailing 400 runes, and a tool call would end the turn with finish_reason='tool_calls' instead of 'stop'
The recipe deliberately does NOT answer the question - this cell locks the ENTRY into waiting, per the scenario description
timeout_seconds is 240 because the driver's deadline starts BEFORE the REPL boot poll and the turn runs against a remote reasoning model

script.text: I want to add a small feature to my project, but I have not told you where it should go. Ask me exactly ONE short clarifying question about which file it belongs in, ending in a question mark, then stop and wait for my answer. Output only that one question and nothing else - plain text, and do not call any tool.

verify: events.jsonl contains a session born in ready shortly after launch (expected to be the transient proc-<PID> pre-session; the store row does not exist until the first user message)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition -> working when the prompt is sent (from the store row's user message, or from the force ready->working bounce if one 2s scan collapses the turn)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition -> waiting on the SAME session once the assistant row lands with finish_reason='stop' and question-ending content
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition -> ready on that session after the waiting transition (the recipe terminates while the session is waiting)
the session's recorded metrics carry non-zero cum_input+output tokens
the session's last observed state is waiting
